clue.text: Absurd aim for a fieldsman

parts.note: absurd means silly
an aim or purpose is the point of something

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder is told his aim is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: SILLY POINT is a cricket fielding position very close to the batsman on the off side, and the name also covers the player standing there.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the player stationed in that close catching position is called by the position's name.

clue.text: Face the team

explanation.surface: Confront the opposing eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is one face of a solid, and a side is also a sporting team.

clue.text: Ring of the cheapest sort?

parts.note: ring here is a telephone call, and the cheapest kind is one within your own area

explanation.surface: Asking which ring costs the least, as if shopping for jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone call to a nearby number used to be charged at the lowest rate.

clue.text: Battle contributing to military prestige?

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A battle that added to an army's glory.
explanation.walkthrough: Ypres in Belgium gave its name to several First World War battles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ypres names a series of First World War engagements in Flanders.

clue.text: More than one player is in new boots

indicators.note: in puts the word is inside the rearranged footwear
new tells us the word boots is made afresh, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer appears in brand-new boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges BOOTS into OBOTS, and 'in' puts IS inside to give OBO-IS-TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboe players are musicians, so a group of them is more than one player.

clue.text: Relatively patronising

parts.note: patronising here means acting as patron, favouring people, and relatively means toward one's own relatives

explanation.surface: Describes someone who is somewhat condescending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patronising' looks like condescending, but it means giving patronage, and 'Relatively' means to relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouritism shown to family members in giving jobs is nepotism, and the adjective describes it.

clue.text: Bat that may be held in the hand

definitions.text: that may be held in the hand

explanation.surface: A bat is something you grip in your hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is a stick for hitting, like a bat, and clubs are a suit of playing cards held in a hand.

clue.text: Look round a ship for a rope

indicators.note: round says the word for look goes around the other pieces

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Search a vessel to find a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's noosed rope for catching cattle has this name.

clue.text: Chinese soup ingredients often include eggs

explanation.surface: A Chinese soup recipe that usually has eggs in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Edible swiftlet nests are a Chinese delicacy for soup; ordinary nests usually hold eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftlet homes made of saliva are a costly soup base, and the homes of birds generally hold eggs.

clue.text: Predator moved to show a sign of distress

indicators.note: moved says the letters of predator are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A hunting animal was emotionally affected and showed it was upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' looks like emotion, but it rearranges PREDATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone crying sheds tears, a visible signal of being upset.

clue.text: Colour scheme for last month — heraldic gold

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated Dec
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A colour scheme chosen for December, using gold from heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the interior decoration of a room, including its colours.

clue.text: He may get a poor press, aptly enough

definitions.text: He may get a poor press, aptly enough

indicators.note: aptly enough hints that the letters of poor press, rearranged, fittingly spell the one who gets it

explanation.surface: A tyrant is likely to receive bad publicity, as he deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of POOR PRESS rearrange into the answer, and the whole clue also describes him: a tyrant gets bad coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant who crushes people is commonly condemned by the media.

clue.text: Tightly packed Wimbledon crowd may well enjoy it

definitions.text: Wimbledon crowd may well enjoy it

explanation.surface: A packed crowd at Wimbledon enjoying the tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; a set is a unit of a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: Things placed near together are densely arranged, and a tight-fought set of tennis thrills spectators.

clue.text: Castles in the air?

parts.note: castles are chess pieces with another name, which is also the name of black birds that fly

explanation.surface: Daydreams, as in the idiom for fanciful plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castles in the air' is an idiom for daydreams, but here castles are chess pieces sharing a name with crows.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess castle is also called by the name of a crow-like bird, found in the sky.

clue.text: In the main, they're disasters for lloyds

definitions.text: In the main, they're disasters for lloyds

parts.words: In the main, they're disasters for lloyds
parts.note: the main is the sea, and Lloyd's of London insures vessels lost there

explanation.surface: Mostly, these are calamities for a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' seems to mean mostly, but the main is the sea; Lloyd's is the London insurance market, not the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessels lost at sea cost marine insurers heavily.

clue.text: Fire stations?

parts.note: stations here are places where a fire sits in a home, not bases for firefighters

explanation.surface: Where the fire brigade is based.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone floor of a fireplace is where a domestic fire burns.

clue.text: Understood vessel could be reserved

parts.note: something understood without being said is tacit
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A container that has been taken as read might be booked.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says little, being quiet and uncommunicative.

clue.text: Damaged blue car may be restored to good condition

definitions.text: may be restored to good condition

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of blue car are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A dented blue car can be repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treatable can be healed or put right.

clue.text: Ideal material for a plinth?

parts.note: a plinth is a base, so the ideal stuff would be the term for common non-precious metals

explanation.surface: Asking what a statue's pedestal should be made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron, lead and the like are common metals, called by a name that puns on the bottom of a statue.

clue.text: Kind of crossing made by Drake's ship

explanation.surface: A sea crossing made aboard Sir Francis Drake's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with lights; Drake's Golden Hind was first called the Pelican.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain has a light-controlled road crossing of this name, and Drake's ship bore it before renaming.

clue.text: In a neat move catch the girl

indicators.note: In says the net goes inside the rearranged letters
move tells us the word neat is shifted into a new order

parts.note: to catch fish is to net them

explanation.surface: With a deft manoeuvre, grab the young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' turns NEAT into NATE, and 'In' puts NET in the middle: NA-NET-TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanette is a female first name, as in the musical No, No, Nanette.

clue.text: Security is brought back in store

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the storehouse

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: brought back says the word is turns round

explanation.surface: Safety has been returned to a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns IS into SI, which 'in' puts inside DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid as a guarantee is a form of security.

clue.text: Customers sit in their own seats in these cinemas

definitions.text: Customers sit in their own seats in these cinemas

parts.words: Customers sit in their own seats in these cinemas
parts.note: the seats are the customers' own car seats, as they watch from their vehicles

explanation.surface: Moviegoers bring their own chairs to the pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air cinemas let viewers watch films from inside their parked cars.

clue.text: Respond to plea to return to the stage

explanation.surface: A performer answers a call for an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to plea to' only links; acting again is a performer coming back on.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer something is to respond to it, and acting again means performing once more.

clue.text: Use one line, or it may need two

explanation.surface: Fish with a single line, or perhaps you need a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To fish with rod and line is to cast for fish, and the geometric figure between two lines has this name.

clue.text: Abominable, if not extreme, form of explosive device

indicators.note: form of says the remaining letters take a new shape
if not extreme says the outermost letters of abominable are dropped

explanation.surface: A dreadful, though not entirely so, kind of bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if not extreme' strips the A and E from ABOMINABLE, leaving BOMINABL, which 'form of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb packed with nails as shrapnel is a terrorist weapon.

clue.text: Growing sources of light

parts.note: the word means both lamps and plant parts that grow underground

explanation.surface: Light sources that are getting brighter or more numerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric lamps give light, and tulip roots sprout in the garden.

clue.text: A mistake whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: whichever way you look at it says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something is an error, however you view it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or gaffe is a slang synonym.

clue.text: Roll up for what suckers buy by the score

definitions.text: what suckers buy by the score

explanation.surface: Gather round to see what fools buy in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll up' sounds like a fairground call, but a roll-up is a hand-rolled smoke; they are sold in packs of twenty to smokers who suck them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-rolled smoke is a homemade version, and packs of twenty smokes are bought by smokers.

clue.text: There's a great deal to this game

parts.note: a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: This game has plenty to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance played by drawing numbers.

clue.text: Appear to make a sound joint

indicators.note: sound says a word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a seam is a joint where two pieces meet

explanation.surface: Try to make a strong, solid connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective, solid, but it signals a word heard: SEAM, a joint, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give the impression of being something.

clue.text: Its members presumably try to improve their services

definitions.text: Its members presumably try to improve their services

parts.words: Its members presumably try to improve their services
parts.note: services here are serves in tennis, which players practise

explanation.surface: An organisation whose staff aim to give better service.
explanation.definitionFit: Players at a racket sports association practise serving the ball.
